newsitem.title: FRANCE: No Algerian wheat buys in next weeks, official says.
newsitem.headline: No Algerian wheat buys in next weeks, official says.

text.p: Algeria will stay out of the wheat market for a while after its reported decision last week to import 275,000 tonnes amid falling world prices, an Algerian cereals authority official said on Monday.
"There is no import tender for the coming days or weeks," the official told Reuters by telephone from Algiers.
Grain traders said last week Algeria had bought 275,000 tonnes of wheat, around half of it American, for shipment in August and the first half of September at around $160 a tonne.
It was one of several deals as mainly North Africa returned to the market after a drop in prices caused by strong harvest progress in the United States.
The Algerian official declined to confirm or deny the deal, which grain exporters reckon is enough to cover the country's needs until at least the end of August.
Nor would he comment on reports that Algeria's import needs would rise this year, although he confirmed that its harvest would be lower than last year.
"Compared to last year there is a deficit," he said of the harvest, while adding it was too early to project imports.
The London-based International Grains Council estimates 1997/98 (July/June) Algerian wheat imports at four million tonnes against 3.2 million tonnes the previous season.
After drought problems earlier this year, it estimates a 1997/98 wheat crop of 1.6 million tonnes compared with 2.4 million tonnes last year.
